text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italian cabinet is due to meet today in order to unveil the centre-left government's three-year economic programme known as the DPEF (all).

* Labour minister Tiziano Treu confirmed the government planned to start negotiations with trade unions and employers on reforming the welfare state on June 18. Trade unions and hard left Communist Refoundation seem quite satisfied with the 1998 budget including 25 trilliom lire of deficit-cutting measures, 15 trillion of which coming from social spending cuts and another 10 trillion lire from increased revenue (all).

* Treasuy minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy was no longer the "ugly duckling" of Europe after Bonn said it would go ahead with plans to revalue gold reserves despite Bundesbank opposition (all).

* European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said he was optimistic Italian state telecommunication holding company Stet would soon pay 60 billion lire to Omnitel to compensate for the fee it paid to become the country's second mobile phone operator (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian average hourly contract wages in April were stable at an annual rate of 4.5 percent, the same rate seen in the previous three months (Sole 24 Ore).

* A study by Italian research institute for economic conditions Isco saw the country's gross domestic product rising 1.1 percent in 1997, while annual consumer price index inflation would average 2.1 percent (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
